column11: the realised Medicare price of the therapy this study is trying to beat, in this exact disease, measured. Syfovre (pegcetacoplan), the first therapy approved for geographic atrophy, took $403,855,394.80 from CMS Medicare Part B over 29,338 beneficiaries in 2024, the book's own drug_demand table (asset row Syfovre, part B, year 2024): $13,765.61 a beneficiary. Part B pays 106% of the average sales price (Social Security Act section 1847A), so the price net of the add-on is $13,765.61 / 1.06 = $12,986.42. The same Syfovre series is already the anchor for this layer's penetration_peak_pct in regn_veopoz.csv, so the price and the reach are now measured on one product and one file. This row is written on the indication rather than on the asset, which forecast.layer_terms reads through LAYER_PRICE_KEYS, because the asset's own price is not this price: see the note
column12: A COMPARATOR, NOT A PRICE THIS PRODUCT HAS, AND THE CHOICE IS THE WHOLE OF THE JUDGEMENT. Veopoz's own price is published and it is two orders of magnitude higher: CMS OPPS Addendum B for October 2026 (effective 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31) carries 'J9376 Inj pozelimab-bbfg, 1 mg K 0911 91.73', a payment limit of $91.73 a milligram, and a dated press report of the launch price agrees to the cent at the 6% add-on, 'Regeneron has set a price of $34,612 per one-use vial for the once-weekly drug - equivalent to around $1.8 million a year at full price' (pharmaphorum, Phil Taylor, 2023-08-21), since $34,612 over 400 mg is $86.53 a milligram and $86.53 x 1.06 = $91.73. At the label's 10 mg/kg weekly maintenance that is millions a patient-year. THAT PRICE CANNOT CROSS INTO THIS INDICATION. It is set for CD55-deficient protein-losing enteropathy, a disease with a few dozen patients in the world, and the layer's own pool is 312,018 Americans. No payer funds an orphan price across a pool that size, and the regimen is different too: NCT06541704 gives pozelimab subcutaneously in combination with cemdisiran, or cemdisiran alone, not the 30 mg/kg intravenous load and 10 mg/kg weekly the Veopoz label describes. No price for that regimen is published anywhere. So the class price is taken. WHICH WAY IT ERRS: low, on two counts. Syfovre's 2024 was its second year on sale and its per-beneficiary spend was still climbing ($4,401.72 in 2023 on 17,414 beneficiaries), so a full year of treatment costs more than $13,765.61. And a systemic subcutaneous regimen that treats both eyes at once should command more than an intravitreal injection priced per eye, not less
